# Report: Poe, “The Philosophy of Composition”

## 1. The question, frozen

The title and first page make one question central: **by what steps did “The Raven” arrive at the shape it has?** Poe turns it into the sharper claim that “no one point in its composition is referrible either to accident or intuition.” So I freeze: *what produced each element of the poem, and was each element forced — or could it have been otherwise?* Range: that one poem, from length to last stanza. Kind: forward, from causes — though Poe answers by reading a finished poem.

Two questions run together here, and I keep them apart: (a) can the steps be recalled? (b) could the parts have been otherwise? Poe treats a yes to (a) as a yes to (b). They differ, and that fusion is where the essay earns most of its apparent tightness.

## 2. The explanation in parts, and its jobs

Parts, in Poe’s words: the intention (suit popular *and* critical taste); about 100 lines (108); Beauty as the poem’s province; melancholy tone; the refrain as pivot; varied application of the refrain; a one-word refrain; long *o* with *r*, giving “Nevermore”; a non-reasoning speaker — parrot, then raven; death of a beautiful woman, lips of a bereaved lover; raven answering the lover’s queries; climax stanza written first; versification (trochaic, octameter acatalectic…); the chamber; window entry with the door-tapping misdirection; tempestuous night; bust of Pallas; fantastic tone dropping to serious; two closing stanzas making the raven emblematical.

Jobs — why this *and not that*: not longer (given); melancholy, not passion or truth (given); “Nevermore,” not another word (given); raven, not parrot or human (given); varied application, not plain repetition (given); that topic (given); chamber, not forest (given); Pallas (given); the window entry (given); no preceding stanza surpassing the climax (added by me); universally appreciable (added); the emblem at the close (added).

**Change list.** Covered: length, tone, refrain word, creature, topic, stanza order, scene, furniture, entry, weather, perch, stanza shape. Godwin’s process is put aside as “not the precise mode.” Left out and said so: “the necessity which… gave rise to the intention of composing a poem that should suit at once the popular and the critical taste,” dismissed as “irrelevant to the poem *per se*.” Left out silently: any change to the world at all. Nothing on the list could be made to move the poem. That is the test Poe never runs.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Intention (popular + critical) | **Fixed** | Owner set it, then declared it outside the question |
| ~100 lines / single sitting | **Held** | Unity of impression, argued from *Paradise Lost* |
| “a hundred lines… it is 108” | **Loose** | Could be 112; nothing turns on the number |
| Beauty as sole province | **Borrowed** | Rests on an unexplained “rule of Art,” untested here |
| Melancholy tone | **Borrowed** | Rests on “all experience has shown,” not tested here |
| Refrain as pivot | **Held** | He inspects the existing refrain, finds it “primitive,” improves it |
| Varied application | **Held** | The engine; strip it and the refrain does nothing |
| One-word refrain | **Held** | Forced by the pull between brevity and varied application |
| Long *o* + *r* | **Held** | Both constraints point at the same shape |
| “Nevermore” | **Held if** | Could be “Evermore” or “Lenore.” Held only by the added emblem job (“Never-ending Remembrance”), which Poe names last |
| Raven, not parrot | **Held** | Swap fails on tone alone; the parrot is “equally capable of speech” |
| Death of a beautiful woman | **Loose** | Asserted as “unquestionably” the most poetical topic; nothing offered to replace it with, so nothing shown to stop a swap |
| Raven’s arrival | **Two routes** | The tempest, or escape from custody; either puts it at the window |
| Climax stanza first | **Held** | Real internal test: no earlier stanza may surpass it |
| The feet/metre | **Borrowed** | Lines “employed before”; Poe says so |
| The stanza combination | **Held** | That combination “has never been attempted” |
| The chamber | **Held if** | Held only by “circumscription of space is absolutely necessary,” itself asserted |
| Richly furnished room | **Idle** | Poe says it follows “in mere pursuance” of the Beauty idea; the poem survives removal |
| Window entry + door misdirection | **Loose** | Job (prolonging curiosity) is real; this way of doing it is not forced |
| Tempestuous night | **Held** | Two jobs: admits the bird, contrasts with serenity within |
| Bust of Pallas | **Held** | Contrast of marble and plumage, plus the lover’s scholarship; “Pallas” itself is loose (Minerva) |
| Fantastic, then serious | **Held** | Contrast, named as deepening the last impression |
| Two closing stanzas | **Held if** | Held only by the “under-current” job — asserted, and the stanzas were added afterwards |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Direction.** Poe is running backwards from the result and presenting it as forward recall. The wording gives it away: “to account for the Raven’s seeking admission”; “the bust was absolutely suggested by the bird.” Reasons are fitted to a finished object, then narrated as if they came first. This is an answer to *what can we tell from the poem*, not to *what produced it*.

**Flip.** Had the first word to suggest itself been “Evermore,” the account has nothing to say. Poe never asks what the poem would have looked like had the effect been different; he only asks what effect each existing part serves.

**Answer hidden in the starting points.** “Beauty is the sole legitimate province”; melancholy “the most legitimate tone”; that topic “unquestionably” the most poetical; “the human thirst for self-torture”; “psychal necessity.” Each is the conclusion wearing the name of a general truth.

**Pairs that pull.** Brevity against sonority — resolved, and this is his tightest joint. Climax vigour against graduation — he gives way on vigour, explicitly. Suggestiveness against “the limits of the real” — resolved by adding two stanzas.

**Patches.** The excluded occasion narrows the claim in silence and removes the one genuine cause. “I pretend to no originality in rhythm or metre” narrows to the combination. No catch-all, so no gauge needed.

**Best rival.** Poe wrote the poem under magazine pressure, then wrote this essay as a second composition selling the same poem as inevitable. No change on his list separates the two, because his list has no changes on it. At this level the two accounts of “what produced the poem” are one.

**Provenance.** *Built:* the refrain scheme, the one-word inference, long *o* + *r*, raven over parrot, the stanza combination — all criticised with the thing in view. *Fitted:* locale, window, tempest, bust, furniture — reasons read off the finished poem. *Asserted:* province, tone, most poetical topic, the first word to present itself, the thirst for self-torture.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. Put the occasion back on the change list, and say what the poem would have been had the demand been different. If nothing changes, “referrible to accident” is dead.
2. For “Nevermore” and “the death of a beautiful woman,” give one change that should have altered the choice and one that should not. Poe supplies neither; those are the two loose bolts worth tightening.

## 6. What this does not show

Passing or failing is not truth. A loose part may be exactly what happened; a held part may be a lucky guess. This run shows which parts are held in place, and by what — nothing more.

## 7. One next step

Take the single word “Nevermore” and write down one change to the world that should have changed it and one that should not.
